FMCSA seeks input on using cameras in place of truck mirrors
item.description: FMCSA has opened a public comment period on a request to let fleets use Safety Vision's View Smart cameras instead of the two side mirrors required on commercial trucks and buses. A notice published Nov. 18 in the Federal Register says Safety Vision is seeking a five-year exemption from the rule requiring a rear-vision mirror on each side, and the agency has not approved the request. The system uses weatherproof cameras on both sides that feed video to screens mounted along the windshield, which the company says offers a wider view, better low-light visibility and alerts for nearby pedestrians or vehicles. Safety Vision has supplied the system to transit bus operators since 2024, though those buses still carry their required mirrors. FMCSA will weigh the application, safety analyses and public comments before deciding whether the system offers safety equal to conventional mirrors. Comments are accepted at Regulations.gov through Dec. 18 under docket FMCSA-2026-3707.

Exception Management in Freight: How AI Is Changing the Work
item.description:
Transport Topics published a feature saying AI is taking over routine freight work, such as load entry and invoice processing, and shifting staff toward exception management. Under that model, automated systems handle routine work, and people step in when a delayed load or billing mismatch needs attention. The article cites industry surveys finding that more than 60% of logistics businesses use some form of AI.
The executives quoted describe assistants that support decisions and flag problems, while agents can act across platforms and resolve some exceptions, though they still need oversight. For companies starting out, the piece recommends beginning with one small, measurable project and expanding gradually once teams understand the tool.

Parts and Accessories Necessary for Safe Operation; Application for Exemption From Safety Vision, LLC
item.description: The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration is asking for public comment on an exemption application from Safety Vision, LLC. The company wants to let motor carriers run commercial motor vehicles with its View Smart camera monitor system in place of the two rear-vision mirrors that the federal rules require. Safety Vision says the system offers an equivalent or greater level of safety, citing a wider field of view, better low-light performance, reduced blind spots and driver alerts. Comments are due December 18, 2026, under docket FMCSA-2026-3707. The notice does not signal what FMCSA will decide, and the agency will grant or deny the exemption after reviewing the application, safety analyses and public comments.

item.title: Commercial Driver's License: Saia LTL Freight; Application for Exemption
item.description:
The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration is asking for public comment on an exemption application from Saia LTL Freight, a company headquartered in John Creek, Georgia. Saia wants commercial learner's permit holders in its driver training program to operate combination vehicles with double trailers while under the direct supervision of a CDL holder with a doubles/triples endorsement. The notice states that it does not indicate what decision FMCSA will ultimately reach.
Saia has requested a 5-year exemption from two rules, 49 CFR 383.93(b)(1) and 383.37(a). According to the filing, approximately 300 trainees a year would use a fleet of about 19 training vehicles. Comments are due December 18, 2026, under docket FMCSA-2026-2642. After reviewing the application, safety analyses and public comments, FMCSA will either grant or deny the request.

item.title: Mack Makes Comparing Truck Configurations Easier
item.description: Mack Trucks has launched MyGarage, a free feature inside its online Truck Builder. Buyers can save, name, search and reopen multiple truck configurations, then send a saved build directly to a Mack dealer when they are ready to talk specifics. Users can also review truck images and selected specifications, and reopen a build to keep refining it. Separately, Truck Builder now lets customers add their company logo to a configured truck, a feature previously limited to Mack dealers.

Q3 2026 Cargo Theft Falls as Losses Rise
item.description:
Verisk CargoNet reported 547 supply chain crime incidents involving cargo across the U.S. and Canada in the third quarter of 2026, down 33% from a year earlier and 19% from the second quarter. Estimated losses still rose 12% to $230.1 million. Fictitious pickups, in which criminals use deception to obtain a shipment, fell only 6% to 138, so their share of reported activity rose to about 25%.
Through September, reported incidents were down 25% year to date, while estimated losses rose 39% to $718.9 million. The average value of stolen goods with a documented value rose 72% to $448,456. CargoNet logged 19 thefts of $1 million or more, compared with nine a year earlier. California accounted for about a third of incidents, and four states made up 57% of the quarterly total. CargoNet also documented fraud schemes in 2026 that used compromised email accounts, internet phone systems and transportation applications, and said theft has historically risen in Q4.

Diesel prices fall to under $6 per gallon
item.description: The national average diesel price fell 19 cents per gallon, from $6.127 to $5.937, according to the weekly report from the United States Energy Information Agency. Every reporting region dropped by double digits. The Central Atlantic had the smallest decline, from $6.412 to $6.309, while the Midwest had the largest, from $6.201 to $5.967. The article links the drop to slipping oil prices. On an early Tuesday, the Associated Press reported that Brent crude edged 49 cents lower to $92.93 a barrel and U.S. benchmark crude slid 51 cents to $86.23 per barrel.

item.title: ATRI extends participation deadline for driver health survey
item.description: The American Transportation Research Institute has extended the deadline for motor carriers and drivers to take part in its survey on the impacts of truck driver health. Responses can now be submitted until Friday, Dec. 4. Carriers are asked for basic fleet-level figures on medical card length, insurance costs and operating KPIs, and they are encouraged to pass the driver questionnaire to their workers. The driver survey takes about five minutes, is anonymous, and covers general health information and experiences staying healthy on the road. The institute said responses are completely confidential.
